newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia shortlists ZCCM sale bidders to six.
newsitem.headline: Zambia shortlists ZCCM sale bidders to six.

text.p: Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) has shortlisted six bidders for final negotitations on the sale of its assets, ZCCM management and the Zambia Privatisation Agency said in a joint statement on Monday.

"ZCCM has invited AUR Resources, the Kafue Consortium (comprising Avmin Ltd, Noranda Mining, Phelps Dodge and the Commonwealth Development Corp), the Binani Group, First Quantam Minerals Ltd, the Metorex Consortium (including Randex and the Crew Group) and Sterlite Industries (India) Ltd, to enter into negotiations in relation to one or more of the asset packages," the statement said.

The ZPA said when bids opened on February 28 that the Kafue Consortium, Metorex, the Binani group and Sterlite Industries had all bid for parts of a package of assets which comprised the Nkana and Nchanga divisions. Both account for half of ZCCM copper production.
The Binani group also bid for parts of Luanshya Division and the Chambishi cobalt plant, which has a nominal capacity of 2,400 tonnes a year.
AUR Resources and Sterlite Industries also put in bids for parts of Luanshya, as well as the Mufulira undergound mine and concentrator, which produced 52,000 tonnes of copper concentrate in 1995/96.
They, along with First Quantam, also bid for the non-operational Chambishi copper mine, which has proven reserves of around 33.5 million tonnes grading 2.55 percent copper.
First Quantam also put in bids for part of Luanshya and Chambishi cobalt and was the only bidder for the Ndola precious metals plant.
The Kafue consortium also bid for the Chambishi cobalt plant.
The ZPA said on Monday that negotiations on the sale of the ZCCM power division would wait until agreements on the sale of the mining and metallurgical assets had been reached.

"The main market for its (the power division) services will be the businesses resulting from the privatisation of the other eight packages. Under these circumstances, it is considered appropriate to have the new customer base finalised before negotiatons on the final condition for the division," the statement said.
The three bids for the power division came from Tractebel, Midlands Power and South African electricity utility Eskom.

Earlier, ZCCM signed an agreement to dispose of the majority stake in the Kansanshi copper mine to Cyprus Amax and signed a memorandum of understanding with a consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa on the development of the Konkola Deep mining project.
